ai.analysis: Gold is down about 1.1% to 4,090 after slicing through 4,100 and yesterday's 4,106.52 low, printing a two-month low in the 4,057-4,066 area. The driver is not the Fed easing, it is the opposite: a Houthi drone strike on Aramco's Shaybah field put Brent back above 111 and WTI near 100, and that oil-inflation impulse has the market pricing an 83-90% chance of a December hike with all 100 economists in the latest Reuters poll now expecting one. What makes today awkward is that everything that normally lifts gold is lifting — the 10-year TIPS real yield is 2.77% versus 2.88% five sessions ago, the 2-year slipped below 4.78%, DXY made a fresh three-week low near 101.50, and Asia sold off hard overnight — and gold ignored all of it for the fifth session running. So the Fed-and-rates backdrop is genuinely mixed: hawkish in what is priced, dovish in what yields are actually doing, and gold has chosen to trade the hawkish half. Reclaim 4,105 and then 4,140 and the macro stack takes the wheel back on the long side; acceptance below 4,057 opens 4,030 and then 4,000, and the 08:30 ET jobless claims print is the first thing today that can settle it.

flags: Correlation break, day 5 and now worse: gold -1.1% to 4,090 (low 4,057-4,066, lowest since mid-Aug on some feeds) while the 10Y TIPS real yield fell to 2.77% (-0.11 vs Oct 13), the 2Y slipped below 4.78%, DXY made a fresh three-week low near 101.50 and Brent went back above $111. Gold is trading the oil-inflation / December-hike story, not its master driver. Note the oil layer scores +1 by the rule (crude bid) while its live transmission into gold today is bearish, via hike bets. Fed layer flipped from +1 yesterday to -1 today: the small drop in Oct 28 hike odds looks like noise against a December hike that 100 of 100 economists in the Oct 16-20 Reuters poll now expect. Retail reset hard overnight — Myfxbook went from 60/40 long with an average long at 4,365 yesterday to 52/48 with the average long at 4,101.51, so the trapped-longs edge that was bearish yesterday has largely been flushed. headline: NEUTRAL — the stack is still BUY-SIDE (+5: real yields -11bp, DXY at a three-week low, Brent $111, COT not crowded) but price has now broken 4,100 AND yesterday's 4,106.52 low to a two-month low, so the correlation break is five sessions old and price has the floor until gold reclaims 4,105-4,140.

mind.line: Macro says buy gold, the tape says sell, and the tape has been right for five sessions — that is a stand-aside, not a fade in either direction. A 4-hour close back above 4,105 and then 4,140 hands it back to the stack on the long side; acceptance below 4,057 says the macro read is the one that is wrong and opens 4,030 then 4,000. Claims at 08:30 ET and any further Saudi/Iran escalation are what resolve it, and both land inside his window.
